description.summary: lets clients hint gesture policy to the compositor

protocol.description:
AsteroidOS-specific protocol used by clients to tell the compositor that they want to handle certain navigation gestures themselves instead of having the compositor consume them.
The compositor is free to honor or ignore these hints.

interface.name: zasteroid_gestures_manager_v1
interface.description: The global entry point. A client binds it and uses it to obtain per-surface gesture objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroys the manager. Previously obtained gesture surfaces are unaffected and must be destroyed separately.

description.summary: get a gesture object for a wl_surface

interface.name: zasteroid_gesture_surface_v1

request.name: destroy
request.description: Returns the surface to default gesture handling.

request.name: set_overrides_system_gestures

description.summary: hint that the client handles its own gestures

request.description:
When enabled is non-zero, the compositor should let edge-swipe and similar navigation gestures reach the client surface instead of consuming them itself (e.g. to close the app or open a system menu).
The hint takes effect on the next surface commit. The default state for a newly created gesture surface is "disabled".

request.name: set_back_from_anywhere

description.summary: let a swipe right from anywhere go back

request.description:
When enabled is non-zero and the system gestures are not overridden, the compositor may take a swipe to the right that starts anywhere on the surface, not only at the edge, as the system back gesture (on a watch: closing the application), as Wear OS does at the root of an application. The client sends it per touch: zero when the touch starts on content of its own that moves sideways.
The default state for a newly created gesture surface is "disabled".

request.name: set_keyboard_open

description.summary: the client shows its full screen keyboard

request.description:
When open is non-zero the client shows a full screen keyboard over its window. As Wear OS does (config_shortPressOnPowerBehavior 5, SHORT_PRESS_POWER_CLOSE_IME_OR_GO_HOME), the compositor then answers a short press of the crown by sending close_keyboard instead of going Home; the next press, with the keyboard closed (the client sends zero), goes Home.
The default state for a newly created gesture surface is "closed". Destroying the object resets it.

event.name: close_keyboard
event.description: The compositor asks the client to close its full screen keyboard (the crown was pressed while set_keyboard_open was non-zero). The client keeps what was typed, as the input method of Wear OS does, and sends set_keyboard_open with zero once the keyboard is closed.
